EAbiTooNew.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EAbiTooNew.description: Manifest schema version above maximum supported — kernel upgrade required
EAbiTooNew.cause: The spirit manifest declares a schema_version higher than the kernel's maximum supported ABI version. This happens when a spirit built for a newer kernel release is deployed onto an older kernel that has not been upgraded.
EAbiTooNew.remediation: Upgrade the MAOS kernel to a version that supports the manifest's declared schema_version. Run `maos version` to check the current kernel ABI ceiling, then consult the release notes for the minimum kernel version that covers the spirit's declared version.

EAbiTooOld.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EAbiTooOld.description: Manifest schema version below N-2 minimum supported — hard refusal
EAbiTooOld.cause: The spirit manifest declares a schema_version that falls below the kernel's N-2 minimum support window. The kernel enforces a hard floor to prevent running dangerously outdated manifests that may lack required security fields.
EAbiTooOld.remediation: Re-author the spirit manifest to target a schema_version within the kernel's supported range. Check `maos manifest validate <manifest>` for the current minimum, then bump the manifest's `schema_version` field and verify all required fields for that version are present.

EClassRequired.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EClassRequired.description: Spirit admitted without required [class] section — manifest malformed or parser bypassed
EClassRequired.cause: The spirit manifest is missing the mandatory `[class]` section. Every spirit must declare its class for the kernel to apply the correct sandbox policy and lifecycle rules. This can also occur if a manifest parser bypass allowed a classless manifest to reach admission.
EClassRequired.remediation:
Add a valid `[class]` section to the spirit manifest TOML. Example: `[class]
kind = "worker"`. Then re-submit the manifest through the standard admission path — never bypass the manifest parser.

ECliBinaryNotFound.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ECliBinaryNotFound.description: CLI binary not found on PATH or at the declared path
ECliBinaryNotFound.cause: The CLI wrapper spirit references an external binary (via the manifest's `binary` or `path` field) that does not exist at the declared filesystem path and is not discoverable on the system PATH.
ECliBinaryNotFound.remediation: Install the required CLI binary and ensure it is either on PATH or referenced by absolute path in the manifest. Verify with `which <binary>` or `ls <declared_path>`. If running in a container, ensure the binary is included in the image.

ECliProbeFailed.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ECliProbeFailed.description: CLI probe subprocess exited non-zero, stdio I/O failure, or adapter-declared probe protocol violated
ECliProbeFailed.cause: The CLI wrapper ran its probe subprocess (typically `<binary> --version` or a custom probe command) and the subprocess exited with a non-zero code, produced unreadable output, or violated the adapter's declared probe protocol.
ECliProbeFailed.remediation: Run the probe command manually outside MAOS to diagnose the failure: e.g. `<binary> --version`. Check that the binary starts correctly, has the right permissions, and that its output matches the adapter's expected probe format. This error is retryable — transient failures (e.g. a locked resource) may resolve on retry.

ECliWrapperRequiresT3.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ECliWrapperRequiresT3.description: Worker ([cli_wrapper]) manifest requested a sandbox tier other than T3; T3 is the only Worker path (below it no scoped egress exists, T4 has no spawn path)
ECliWrapperRequiresT3.cause: The Worker manifest's `[sandbox]` `tier` resolves to a tier other than `T3` (`T0`, `T1`, `T2` or `T4`). A `[cli_wrapper]` Worker runs only inside a verified T3 rootless container (`--network=none`, `--read-only`, `--cap-drop=ALL`, `--user=65534:65534`), whose only egress is the daemon's proxy socket at `/proxy/egress.sock`. Below `T3` no scoped egress or credential custody exists for a Worker; `T4` has no spawn path. `maos run` refuses the manifest at load, before any probe or spawn. `T3` is not the highest tier, and there is no `hardened` tier: the parser accepts only `T0`–`T4`.
ECliWrapperRequiresT3.remediation: Set `tier = "T3"` in the manifest's `[sandbox]` table, or omit `[sandbox]` (a Worker requests `T3` by default). The operator must also grant `T3` for the manifest's `command` and `[author]` `name` in the `MAOS_HOST_GRANTS` file; otherwise admission fails with `ECliWrapperTierNotGranted`.

ECliWrapperTierNotGranted.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ECliWrapperTierNotGranted.description: Manifest requested sandbox tier not granted by host-side grant allowlist — fail-closed, no silent downgrade
ECliWrapperTierNotGranted.cause: The spirit manifest requests a sandbox tier (e.g. t3) that the host-side grant allowlist does not include. The kernel enforces fail-closed behavior — it will not silently downgrade to a lower tier.
ECliWrapperTierNotGranted.remediation: Add the requested sandbox tier to the host's grant allowlist configuration. Locate the grant allowlist (typically in the MAOS host config or deployment policy) and add the spirit's identity or class to the t3 grant list. Re-deploy after updating the allowlist.

EComplianceRejection::ContextDrift.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EComplianceRejection::ContextDrift.description: Runtime execution-context drifted from the attested ComplianceClaim fingerprint
EComplianceRejection::ContextDrift.cause: During runtime, the execution context (environment fingerprint, resource bindings, or host state) changed in a way that no longer matches the fingerprint attested in the ComplianceClaim. This indicates the compliance invariant was violated after initial admission.
EComplianceRejection::ContextDrift.remediation: Investigate what changed in the execution environment since the ComplianceClaim was issued. Common triggers include host reconfiguration, resource re-binding, or container migration. Re-attest the ComplianceClaim against the current context fingerprint and re-submit the spirit.

EComplianceRejection::ExpiredClaim.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EComplianceRejection::ExpiredClaim.description: ComplianceClaim carried an expires_at_unix_ms in the past
EComplianceRejection::ExpiredClaim.cause: The ComplianceClaim's `expires_at_unix_ms` timestamp is in the past relative to the kernel's clock. Claims are time-bounded to prevent stale attestations from being replayed.
EComplianceRejection::ExpiredClaim.remediation: Re-issue the ComplianceClaim with a fresh `expires_at_unix_ms` value. Ensure the claim-issuing service and the MAOS kernel have synchronized clocks (NTP). If clock skew is suspected, check `timedatectl` or equivalent on both the issuer and the kernel host.

EComplianceRejection::MalformedClaim.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EComplianceRejection::MalformedClaim.description: ComplianceClaim could not be decoded, was missing a required field, or carried an unknown enum value
EComplianceRejection::MalformedClaim.cause: The ComplianceClaim payload could not be decoded (invalid encoding), was missing a required field (e.g. `issuer`, `subject`, `expires_at_unix_ms`), or contained an unrecognized enum variant that the kernel cannot interpret.
EComplianceRejection::MalformedClaim.remediation: Validate the ComplianceClaim against the expected schema before submission. Ensure all required fields are present and that enum values match the kernel's known set. Use a JSON/CBOR validator to check encoding integrity.

EComplianceRejection::SignatureInvalid.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EComplianceRejection::SignatureInvalid.description: ComplianceClaim Ed25519 signature verification failed (or signing_alg unsupported)
EComplianceRejection::SignatureInvalid.cause: The Ed25519 signature on the ComplianceClaim failed cryptographic verification. This can occur if the claim was tampered with in transit, signed with a wrong or rotated key, or uses an unsupported signing algorithm.
EComplianceRejection::SignatureInvalid.remediation: Verify that the signing key used to produce the ComplianceClaim matches the public key the kernel trusts. Check the key fingerprint with the compliance authority. If keys were rotated, update the kernel's trusted-key store and re-sign the claim.

ECrossWallRecallDenied.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ECrossWallRecallDenied.description: Cross-wall log recall lacks a fresh directional consent grant
ECrossWallRecallDenied.cause: Cross-wall log recall could not prove fresh directional consent: the grant is absent or reversed, the consent provider or state is unavailable or stale, or the remote read port is not configured.
ECrossWallRecallDenied.remediation: Inspect the refusal reason. Obtain a fresh grant for the requested team and log-recall direction, restore the consent provider or state if unavailable, and configure the remote read port before retrying. Do not bypass the consent check.

EEgressNotGranted.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EEgressNotGranted.description: The Worker requests a host:port destination outside its host grant
EEgressNotGranted.cause: The Worker manifest's `[cli_wrapper]` `egress` lists a `host:port` destination that the operator's host grant for this `command` and `[author]` `name` does not permit. Manifest egress must be a subset of the grant's `permitted_egress_destinations`, where a bare host grants only `host:443`. `maos run` refuses the Worker at admission, before any probe or spawn; no destination is ever added from the manifest.
EEgressNotGranted.remediation: Remove the destination from the manifest's `egress`, or have the operator add it to the matching `[[grant]]` entry's `permitted_egress_destinations` in the `MAOS_HOST_GRANTS` file (write `host:port` for any port other than 443), then rerun `maos run`.

EEgressProxyUnavailable.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EEgressProxyUnavailable.description: A non-empty Worker egress policy requires an available daemon-owned proxy
EEgressProxyUnavailable.cause: The Worker manifest declares a non-empty `[cli_wrapper]` `egress`, but this `maos` root has no egress proxy: the platform is not Unix, no MAOS home could be resolved (`MAOS_HOME` and `HOME` unset), the proxy failed to start (`maos: egress proxy unavailable: …` on stderr at boot), or the root is shutting down. A Worker's only route to the network is that proxy, so admission refuses rather than spawn a Worker whose declared egress cannot be enforced.
EEgressProxyUnavailable.remediation: Run the Worker on Linux from a root that can resolve its MAOS home and create its private `egress` directory under it; check boot stderr for the `egress proxy unavailable` line and fix the reported cause. A Worker that needs no network can drop `egress` from its manifest instead.

EHaltContinuityViolation.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EHaltContinuityViolation.description: Hot-swap halt-protocol schema mismatch — successor does not support predecessor halt version (I14)
EHaltContinuityViolation.cause: During a hot-swap, the successor spirit does not support the halt-protocol schema version that the predecessor used to serialize its halt state. This violates invariant I14 which requires halt-protocol continuity across swaps.
EHaltContinuityViolation.remediation: Ensure the successor spirit's manifest declares support for the predecessor's halt-protocol version in its `halt_versions_supported` list. If the predecessor used halt protocol v2, the successor must list v2 (or a superset). Update the successor manifest and re-attempt the hot-swap.

EIntentLineageBroken.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EIntentLineageBroken.description: Cross-Spirit frame has empty intent_lineage on non-human origin (I14 consent-laundering guard)
EIntentLineageBroken.cause: A cross-spirit IAC (inter-agent communication) frame arrived with an empty `intent_lineage` field, but its origin is non-human. Invariant I14 requires that all machine-originated frames carry a non-empty intent lineage to prevent consent-laundering — one spirit impersonating a human origin to bypass approval gates.
EIntentLineageBroken.remediation: Ensure the sending spirit populates the `intent_lineage` field on every outbound IAC frame. The lineage must trace back to the original human-approved intent. Review the sending spirit's IAC dispatch logic to confirm it propagates lineage from its own inbound frames.

EManifestSchemaConflict.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EManifestSchemaConflict.description: Manifest declares both [class] and [cli_wrapper] — mutually exclusive per architecture §6.7
EManifestSchemaConflict.cause: The spirit manifest contains both a `[class]` section and a `[cli_wrapper]` section. Per architecture §6.7 these are mutually exclusive — a spirit is either a native class-based spirit or a CLI wrapper, never both.
EManifestSchemaConflict.remediation: Remove one of the conflicting sections from the manifest. If the spirit wraps an external CLI binary, keep `[cli_wrapper]` and remove `[class]`. If it is a native spirit, keep `[class]` and remove `[cli_wrapper]`.

EMigratorMissing.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EMigratorMissing.description: No state-transfer migrator registered for predecessor→successor class+version pair
EMigratorMissing.cause: A hot-swap was attempted between a predecessor and successor spirit, but no state-transfer migrator is registered for that specific class+version pair. The kernel cannot transfer runtime state without a matching migrator.
EMigratorMissing.remediation: Register a migrator for the predecessor→successor class+version pair in the spirit registry. Implement the `StateMigrator` trait for the transition and register it before attempting the hot-swap. Check `maos registry list-migrators` to see what is currently registered.

EMigratorMissing_PrecheckOutcome.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EMigratorMissing_PrecheckOutcome.description: Precheck verdict: migrator missing for the hot-swap candidate
EMigratorMissing_PrecheckOutcome.cause: The hot-swap precheck phase detected that no migrator is registered for the candidate swap. This is the precheck-phase equivalent of EMigratorMissing — it fires before the actual swap is attempted to provide an early failure signal.
EMigratorMissing_PrecheckOutcome.remediation: Register the missing migrator for the predecessor→successor transition before re-running the precheck. This is identical to the EMigratorMissing remediation — implement and register a `StateMigrator` for the specific class+version pair.

EModelProvenanceMissing.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EModelProvenanceMissing.description: Spirit class requires model-provenance but the [model_provenance] manifest section is absent at admission (NFR-Comp-5 / SB-1047)
EModelProvenanceMissing.cause: The admission policy requires model provenance, but the Spirit manifest has no [model_provenance] section. Absence is allowed only when the policy does not require it.
EModelProvenanceMissing.remediation: Add a valid [model_provenance] section with covered_model_id, schema-valid training_data_lineage references, and last_eval_timestamp backed by the actual model evaluation, then resubmit through admission. Do not disable the requirement to admit an undocumented model.

EModelProvenanceStale.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EModelProvenanceStale.description: Declared model-provenance last_eval_timestamp is older than the operator-configured staleness window (D6 — presence necessary but not sufficient)
EModelProvenanceStale.cause: The declared model-provenance last_eval_timestamp is older than the admission policy's configured max_age_secs relative to now_unix_secs. The staleness check runs only when the operator supplies a maximum age.
EModelProvenanceStale.remediation: Compare the reported evaluation time, admission time, and maximum age with the real evaluation record and clock. Perform a fresh evaluation when required and update last_eval_timestamp to that evaluation's actual time before resubmitting; do not just advance the timestamp to evade the age check.

EOrchestratorDispatchRawOutput.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EOrchestratorDispatchRawOutput.description: Orchestrator dispatch references raw worker output instead of a distillate (FR21)
EOrchestratorDispatchRawOutput.cause: An orchestrator spirit's dispatch references raw worker output directly instead of referencing a distillate (per FR21). Raw output must be distilled before it can be dispatched to downstream consumers, to ensure safety and compliance review.
EOrchestratorDispatchRawOutput.remediation: Update the orchestrator's dispatch logic to reference a distillate ID rather than a raw output ID. Ensure the worker's output has been processed through the distillation pipeline before the orchestrator dispatches it. Check the orchestrator's IAC frame construction code.

EOutputShapeAdapterMismatch.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EOutputShapeAdapterMismatch.description: ADR-021: observed CLI output shape does not match declared output_shape_version — admission refused
EOutputShapeAdapterMismatch.cause: The CLI wrapper's actual output (observed during the probe or first invocation) does not match the `output_shape_version` declared in the manifest. Per ADR-021 the kernel enforces shape consistency at admission time to prevent downstream parsing failures.
EOutputShapeAdapterMismatch.remediation: Update the manifest's `output_shape_version` to match the CLI binary's actual output format, or update the CLI binary to produce output matching the declared shape. Run the CLI manually and compare its output structure against the declared shape adapter.

EOutputShapeAdapterNotRegistered.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EOutputShapeAdapterNotRegistered.description: Output-shape adapter not registered in the Spirit registry
EOutputShapeAdapterNotRegistered.cause: The spirit manifest references an `output_shape_version` whose adapter is not registered in the Spirit registry. The kernel cannot parse the CLI output without a matching adapter.
EOutputShapeAdapterNotRegistered.remediation: Register the output-shape adapter in the Spirit registry before submitting the manifest. Implement the adapter for the declared `output_shape_version` and register it. Alternatively, change the manifest to reference an already-registered shape version.

EPinMismatch::FingerprintCollision.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EPinMismatch::FingerprintCollision.description: Fingerprint insertion refused — another peer already holds the fingerprint as a current pin or open rotation generation
EPinMismatch::FingerprintCollision.cause: A proposed first-contact pin, operator-approved re-pin, or next rotation fingerprint is already held by another peer as a current pin or open rotation generation. Opening a rotation window with the peer's own current fingerprint is also refused.
EPinMismatch::FingerprintCollision.remediation: Compare the reported peer, colliding_peer, and fingerprint against the trusted peer configuration. Give each peer a distinct verified identity; for rotation, use a new fingerprint different from the current pin. Investigate unexpected key reuse before retrying the trust or rotation operation.

EPinMismatch::Invalidated.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EPinMismatch::Invalidated.description: TOFU pin invalidated for peer (Spirit restart, manual invalidation)
EPinMismatch::Invalidated.cause: The TOFU (Trust On First Use) pin for a peer is invalidated. Usually the peer Spirit restarted: its frame carried a boot nonce different from the pinned one (NFR-Rel-6 restart detection), the certificate identity is unchanged, and re-pin consent is required. The pin can also be manually invalidated, or a rotation-window or first-contact operation can be refused against an existing or invalidated pin.
EPinMismatch::Invalidated.remediation: After a peer restart, confirm the restart with the peer's operator and obtain its new boot nonce (decimal) out of band. On the receiving host's `cohort-a2a-daemon` door run `maosctl a2a repin list`, then `maosctl a2a repin approve <peer> --boot-nonce <N>` within 300 s of the detection: it re-pins the SAME pinned fingerprint with nonce N and writes an Approval Decision Log row first. The re-pin is held in memory only; a restart of the receiving daemon rebuilds pins from `[[tcp.peer_pins]]`. The alternative recovery is to correct that row's `boot_nonce` and restart the receiving host. If the restart was unexpected, investigate a possible compromise before approving; refuse with `maosctl a2a repin reject <peer> --boot-nonce <N>`.

EPinMismatch::Mismatch.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EPinMismatch::Mismatch.description: TOFU pin mismatch for peer — pinned fingerprint does not match observed
EPinMismatch::Mismatch.cause: The observed cryptographic fingerprint of a peer spirit does not match the previously pinned fingerprint (TOFU). This is a potential man-in-the-middle indicator — something is presenting a different identity than what was trusted on first contact.
EPinMismatch::Mismatch.remediation: Do NOT blindly accept the new fingerprint. Investigate why the peer's fingerprint changed. If the peer was legitimately re-keyed, verify through an out-of-band channel and update the pin. If the change is unexplained, treat it as a potential security incident and escalate to the security team.

EPinMismatch::NotPinned.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
EPinMismatch::NotPinned.description: No TOFU pin recorded for peer — first-contact not yet attempted
EPinMismatch::NotPinned.cause: No TOFU pin exists for the target peer. Pins are configured, not learned: each one is loaded at transport bind from a `[[tcp.peer_pins]]` row in this host's configuration, and an unpinned peer is refused rather than trusted on first contact.
EPinMismatch::NotPinned.remediation: Verify the peer's leaf-certificate SHA-256 fingerprint and current boot nonce out of band, add a `[[tcp.peer_pins]]` row for it (`peer_id`, `fingerprint`, decimal `boot_nonce`) to this host's configuration, and restart this process so the pin store is rebuilt from config. No runtime command creates a first pin; `maosctl a2a repin` only re-arms an existing pin.

ERegionTagInvalid.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ERegionTagInvalid.description: Operator-supplied region tag failed the frozen ascii-v1 grammar (AC-12), rejected before any key derivation
ERegionTagInvalid.cause: An operator-supplied region tag is invalid after trimming whitespace and ASCII lowercasing: its length is outside 2..=32 bytes or it contains characters other than lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens.
ERegionTagInvalid.remediation: Correct the region tag in operator configuration or MAOS_REGION_HOME to 2..=32 ASCII characters from [a-z0-9-], then retry. Region tags are canonicalized by trimming and ASCII lowercasing; underscores, Unicode characters, and embedded spaces remain invalid.

ERegionViolation.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ERegionViolation.description: Foreign-region data detected on a read/verify/enforcement path — region pinning fail-closed (NFR-Comp-4 / PIPL §40)
ERegionViolation.cause: A region-pinned read or write received data tagged for a different region, or foreign-origin data without a verifiable region tag. The enforcement path rejects it instead of trusting data outside the configured home region.
ERegionViolation.remediation: Inspect the expected and found regions and the operation detail. Route the operation to data bound to the configured home region, or restore its verifiable region metadata from a trusted source. Do not relabel foreign data or disable pinning to force the operation through.

ERespawnWithContextUnsupported.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ERespawnWithContextUnsupported.description: recovery_policy=respawn_with_context deferred to Epic 10 / NFR-Rel-3 HSIS — admission fails closed
ERespawnWithContextUnsupported.cause: The spirit manifest sets `recovery_policy = "respawn_with_context"`, but this recovery mode is not yet implemented — it is deferred to Epic 10 / NFR-Rel-3 (HSIS). The kernel fails closed rather than silently ignoring the unsupported policy.
ERespawnWithContextUnsupported.remediation: Change the manifest's `recovery_policy` to a supported value (e.g. `"respawn"` or `"halt"`). The `respawn_with_context` mode will be available in a future release. Monitor the MAOS roadmap for Epic 10 delivery.

ESkillProposal::EmptyDiff.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillProposal::EmptyDiff.description: Revision proposal proposed_diff must be non-empty (FR57)
ESkillProposal::EmptyDiff.cause: A skill revision proposal was submitted with an empty `proposed_diff` field. Per FR57, every revision proposal must contain a non-empty diff describing what changed.
ESkillProposal::EmptyDiff.remediation: Populate the `proposed_diff` field with the actual changes before submitting the revision proposal. The diff should describe the content modifications between the current skill version and the proposed revision.

ESkillProposal::EmptyTargetId.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillProposal::EmptyTargetId.description: Revision proposal target_skill_id must be non-empty
ESkillProposal::EmptyTargetId.cause: A skill revision proposal was submitted with an empty `target_skill_id` field. The proposal must identify which skill it targets.
ESkillProposal::EmptyTargetId.remediation: Set the `target_skill_id` field to the non-empty identifier of the skill being revised. Use `maos skill list` to find valid skill IDs in the registry.

ESkillProposal::InvalidTargetIdCharset.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillProposal::InvalidTargetIdCharset.description: Revision proposal target_skill_id contains invalid characters
ESkillProposal::InvalidTargetIdCharset.cause: The `target_skill_id` in the revision proposal contains characters outside the allowed set. Skill IDs must conform to the charset rules (typically lowercase alphanumeric, hyphens, and dots).
ESkillProposal::InvalidTargetIdCharset.remediation: Correct the `target_skill_id` to use only allowed characters: lowercase letters (a-z), digits (0-9), hyphens (-), and dots (.). Remove or replace any uppercase letters, spaces, underscores, or special characters.

ESkillProposal::InvalidTargetVersion.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillProposal::InvalidTargetVersion.description: Revision proposal target_version is not valid semver
ESkillProposal::InvalidTargetVersion.cause: The `target_version` field in the revision proposal is not a valid semver string (e.g. `1.2.3`). The kernel requires strict semver for all version references.
ESkillProposal::InvalidTargetVersion.remediation: Fix the `target_version` to be a valid semver string (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, e.g. `1.0.0`). Pre-release and build metadata are allowed per semver spec (e.g. `1.0.0-beta.1`). Do not use partial versions like `1.0` or non-numeric segments.

ESkillQueue::AlreadyDecided.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::AlreadyDecided.cause: The selected queue entry is already Admitted or Rejected rather than Pending.
ESkillQueue::AlreadyDecided.remediation: Show the entry and reconcile approval rows before preparing a decision. Submit a new version or revision instead of rewriting a terminal decision.

ESkillQueue::AmbiguousEntry.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::AmbiguousEntry.description: Entry id required for a shared skill id
ESkillQueue::AmbiguousEntry.cause: Multiple queued versions or proposals share the selected skill id; first-match selection could decide the wrong payload.
ESkillQueue::AmbiguousEntry.remediation: Select an exact entry id from the queue list. Revision approval targets end in #entry_id and never share the base skill's decision target.

ESkillQueue::AuthoredIdTooLong.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::AuthoredIdTooLong.description: Authored skill identifier exceeds the shared length limit
ESkillQueue::AuthoredIdTooLong.cause: An authored skill id exceeds the operator door's 128-byte identifier boundary.
ESkillQueue::AuthoredIdTooLong.remediation: Choose a lowercase namespaced id of at most 128 ASCII bytes before submitting; do not truncate an existing identity.

ESkillQueue::CapabilityEscalation.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::CapabilityEscalation.description: Skill requirements exceed the author's declared actions
ESkillQueue::CapabilityEscalation.cause: At least one required_capabilities entry is not an exact member of the root-supplied declared scope action keys.
ESkillQueue::CapabilityEscalation.remediation: Remove undeclared requirements or change and re-admit the Spirit manifest through normal operator admission. Skill documents never grant authority.

ESkillQueue::DuplicateSkillId.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::DuplicateSkillId.description: A conflicting pending submission or already-recorded canonical entry identity exists
ESkillQueue::DuplicateSkillId.cause: New documents are bounded to one Pending entry per skill id. Revisions are bounded to one Pending entry per target and full author provenance (class, pid, boot nonce). Exact canonical entry identities cannot be replayed, including after a terminal decision.
ESkillQueue::DuplicateSkillId.remediation: Wait for the pending entry's operator decision before submitting a distinct payload. Use an advancing document version or a new revision payload rather than replaying an entry; select exact entry ids for coexisting revisions.

ESkillQueue::EntryNotFound.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::EntryNotFound.cause: No queued entry matches the requested entry id or skill id.
ESkillQueue::EntryNotFound.remediation: List the queue in the intended data home and use a returned exact entry id. No decision or payload mutation occurred.

ESkillQueue::EvidenceMismatch.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::EvidenceMismatch.description: Telemetry evidence pid differs from author provenance
ESkillQueue::EvidenceMismatch.cause: The root-assembled telemetry report pid differs from the fixed author pid.
ESkillQueue::EvidenceMismatch.remediation: Obtain evidence from the root aggregator for the bound pid since its bind instant. Do not coerce the pid or accept Spirit-supplied evidence.

ESkillQueue::ForeignNamespace.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::ForeignNamespace.description: Authored skill id is outside the author's namespace
ESkillQueue::ForeignNamespace.cause: An authored id does not begin with the root-resolved author class followed by a dot.
ESkillQueue::ForeignNamespace.remediation: Use an id in the author's own class namespace; do not alter provenance or bypass the root-bound port. Nothing is enqueued.

ESkillQueue::InvalidStoredEntry.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::InvalidStoredEntry.description: Corrupt persisted skill identity or payload
ESkillQueue::InvalidStoredEntry.cause: Stored identity, payload or provenance violates queue invariants, including SHA mismatch, duplicate live entry id, missing author payload or mismatched document id/version.
ESkillQueue::InvalidStoredEntry.remediation: Preserve the original file and restore validated data. Do not recompute hashes to legitimize altered content. V1 label-only entries remain explicitly legacy.

ESkillQueue::NonFiniteEvidence.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::NonFiniteEvidence.description: Revision evidence cannot be durably represented
ESkillQueue::NonFiniteEvidence.cause: Revision telemetry contains a non-finite f32 halt value or threshold that cannot round-trip through durable JSON.
ESkillQueue::NonFiniteEvidence.remediation: Correct the telemetry producer and submit only finite evidence; preserve the existing queue and never replace non-finite measurements with fabricated values.

ESkillQueue::PrincipalDataRefused.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::PrincipalDataRefused.description: Payload contains an indexed principal id
ESkillQueue::PrincipalDataRefused.cause: The document or diff contains a token-bounded principal id indexed to the root-fixed author pid; the queue is outside forget's erasure reach.
ESkillQueue::PrincipalDataRefused.remediation: Remove personal identifiers before resubmission. Do not echo the matched principal in a refusal receipt. Unindexed personal data remains a stated limit of this check.

ESkillQueue::Proposal.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::Proposal.cause: A live or stored revision has an invalid target id/version or an empty diff; the wrapped ESkillProposal preserves the precise cause.
ESkillQueue::Proposal.remediation: Correct the proposal before resubmitting. Keep root-attached evidence and opaque diff semantics; approval does not apply the diff.

ESkillQueue::Schema.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::Schema.cause: A live or stored authored document failed strict maos.skill.v1 validation; the wrapped ESkillSchema identifies the precise failure.
ESkillQueue::Schema.remediation: Correct the document according to the schema cause before resubmitting. Restore persisted invalid content from validated data rather than silently discarding it.

ESkillQueue::StaleTargetVersion.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::StaleTargetVersion.description: Target version is stale or authored version does not advance
ESkillQueue::StaleTargetVersion.cause: A proposal names a version other than the highest admitted owned semver, or a new authored document does not strictly exceed every same-id non-revision queue entry in any state and every discovered package version.
ESkillQueue::StaleTargetVersion.remediation: Read current owned entries before proposing. Submit authored documents above all previous non-revision and discovered versions, including rejected drafts; approval of an opaque revision alone does not apply a diff.

ESkillQueue::TargetNotOwned.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::TargetNotOwned.description: Revision target is not an admitted skill authored by this class
ESkillQueue::TargetNotOwned.cause: The target has no admitted AuthorSelf document whose provenance class matches the root-resolved author class; package and legacy entries do not establish ownership.
ESkillQueue::TargetNotOwned.remediation: Select an admitted owned skill from own_entries. Have the operator admit the original authored document first; nothing is enqueued on refusal.

ESkillQueue::UnknownEntryPath.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillQueue::UnknownEntryPath.cause: A stored entry label is not package_shipped, author_self or revision_proposal. Unknown v1 labels also refuse migration.
ESkillQueue::UnknownEntryPath.remediation: Preserve the queue and restore validated provenance. Never substitute PackageShipped or proceed with an invented empty queue after load failure.

ESkillSchema::EmptyBody.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillSchema::EmptyBody.description: Skill body must be present (non-empty markdown after frontmatter fence)
ESkillSchema::EmptyBody.cause: The skill document has no content after the TOML frontmatter fence. A skill must contain non-empty markdown body text that describes its behavior.
ESkillSchema::EmptyBody.remediation: Add markdown content after the closing `---` fence of the TOML frontmatter. The body should describe the skill's purpose, triggers, and behavior. Even a minimal description is required.

ESkillSchema::EmptyId.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillSchema::EmptyId.cause: The skill's TOML frontmatter has an `id` field that is empty or contains only whitespace. Every skill must have a non-empty identifier.
ESkillSchema::EmptyId.remediation: Set the `id` field in the TOML frontmatter to a non-empty value. Example: `id = "my-skill-name"`. The ID must also conform to charset rules (lowercase alphanumeric, hyphens, dots).

ESkillSchema::EmptyName.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillSchema::EmptyName.cause: The skill's TOML frontmatter has a `name` field that is empty or contains only whitespace. Every skill must have a human-readable display name.
ESkillSchema::EmptyName.remediation: Set the `name` field in the TOML frontmatter to a non-empty human-readable string. Example: `name = "My Skill Name"`. The name is used for display purposes in the skill registry.

ESkillSchema::InvalidIdCharset.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillSchema::InvalidIdCharset.description: Skill id contains invalid characters (allowed: a-z, 0-9, '-', '.')
ESkillSchema::InvalidIdCharset.cause: The skill's `id` field contains characters outside the allowed set. Only lowercase letters (a-z), digits (0-9), hyphens (-), and dots (.) are permitted.
ESkillSchema::InvalidIdCharset.remediation: Rename the skill ID to use only allowed characters. Replace uppercase letters with lowercase, spaces/underscores with hyphens. Example: `My_Skill` → `my-skill`.

ESkillSchema::InvalidSemver.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillSchema::InvalidSemver.description: Skill version is not a valid semver string
ESkillSchema::InvalidSemver.cause: The skill's `version` field in the TOML frontmatter is not a valid semver string. The kernel strictly validates version strings at parse time.
ESkillSchema::InvalidSemver.remediation: Set the `version` field to a valid semver string: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (e.g. `version = "1.0.0"`). Partial versions like `1.0` or non-numeric versions like `v1` are not accepted.

ESkillSchema::MissingFence.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillSchema::MissingFence.description: maos.skill.v1 document missing the --- TOML frontmatter fence
ESkillSchema::MissingFence.cause: The skill document is missing the `---` TOML frontmatter fence. The `maos.skill.v1` format requires a fenced TOML block at the top of the document.
ESkillSchema::MissingFence.remediation:
Add the TOML frontmatter fence at the top of the skill document. The document must start with `---` followed by TOML key-value pairs and end with `---` before the markdown body. Example:
```
---
id = "my-skill"
name = "My Skill"
version = "1.0.0"
---
Skill body here.
```

ESkillSchema::TomlParse.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillSchema::TomlParse.description: TOML frontmatter failed to parse (malformed syntax, missing required field, wrong value type)
ESkillSchema::TomlParse.cause: The TOML content within the frontmatter fences failed to parse. This is caused by malformed TOML syntax (unclosed quotes, invalid escapes), a missing required field, or a field with the wrong value type (e.g. string where integer expected).
ESkillSchema::TomlParse.remediation: Validate the TOML frontmatter with a TOML linter (e.g. `taplo check`). Fix any syntax errors, add missing required fields, and ensure value types match the schema. Common issues: unquoted strings, missing commas in arrays, bare keys with special characters.

ESkillSchema::UnknownField.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillSchema::UnknownField.description: Unknown field in TOML frontmatter — deny_unknown_fields rejects it
ESkillSchema::UnknownField.cause: The TOML frontmatter contains a field name that is not recognized by the skill schema. The schema uses `deny_unknown_fields` to reject any extraneous keys, preventing silent misconfiguration.
ESkillSchema::UnknownField.remediation: Remove the unrecognized field from the TOML frontmatter. Check the skill schema documentation for the list of valid fields. Common mistakes: typos in field names (e.g. `verson` instead of `version`), or fields from a newer schema version not yet supported.

ESkillStore::InvalidEntry.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillStore::InvalidEntry.description: Typed stored or submitted entry validation refusal
ESkillStore::InvalidEntry.cause: The durable API rejected a submitted or stored entry with a typed ESkillQueue cause such as failed namespace/ownership, principal data, escalation or corrupt payload.
ESkillStore::InvalidEntry.remediation: Handle the wrapped queue variant without string fallback. Preserve unreadable queues and journal non-personal live refusal receipts at the root-fixed author pid.

ESkillStore::Io.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillStore::Io.description: Filesystem I/O failure reading or writing the durable skill-queue cache (queue.json)
ESkillStore::Io.cause: The skill-queue store encountered a filesystem error reading queue.json or creating, writing, syncing, or renaming its atomic replacement. A nonexistent queue file alone is treated as an empty queue, not this error.
ESkillStore::Io.remediation: Inspect the underlying I/O error and <maos_home>/skills/queue.json (MAOS_HOME, otherwise HOME/.maos). Restore directory access, writable storage, and available space as appropriate; preserve existing queues and journal the one-time validated migration from the former data-home path.

ESkillStore::Json.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillStore::Json.description: The durable payload queue could not be strictly serialized or deserialized
ESkillStore::Json.cause: Invalid JSON, missing required v2 identity/provenance/payload fields, unknown fields or incompatible types prevent strict serialization/deserialization. V1 label-only entries require the explicit versioned migration.
ESkillStore::Json.remediation: Preserve queue.json and inspect the underlying JSON error. Restore validated payload data or repair it deliberately before submitting or deciding. Discovery and the transparency log cannot reconstruct documents, diffs or telemetry evidence: never rebuild an empty queue over a corrupt payload store.

ESkillStore::MaterializeCollision.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillStore::MaterializeCollision.cause: The destination skill file is not recognized as admitted document bytes owned by the same author class; byte equality to an unadmitted draft alone does not establish ownership.
ESkillStore::MaterializeCollision.remediation: Preserve and inspect the existing file, then resolve the collision explicitly before reconciliation. Do not overwrite foreign content merely because a queue decision committed. Revision decisions never materialize.

ESkillStore::NoDataHome.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillStore::NoDataHome.cause: Neither MAOS_HOME nor HOME identifies a private home, or authored admission was called without an explicit materialization directory. Persisted payloads have no tmp fallback.
ESkillStore::NoDataHome.remediation: Configure an absolute MAOS_HOME or the intended user's HOME. The queue uses <maos_home>/skills/queue.json; admitted documents use HOME/.maos/skills. Daemon boot warns and leaves authoring unavailable rather than blocking unrelated modes; explicit test paths remain supported.

ESkillStore::UnknownSchemaVersion.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESkillStore::UnknownSchemaVersion.description: queue.json carries an unknown/absent schema_version (hard error — no best-effort parse; the version stamp is a tripwire)
ESkillStore::UnknownSchemaVersion.cause: The queue declares neither maos.skill-queue.v2 nor the supported v1 migration format, or omits schema_version. Unknown versions are never interpreted as the current schema.
ESkillStore::UnknownSchemaVersion.remediation: Use compatible software and preserve the original payload file. Restore a valid backup if necessary; do not relabel an unknown schema, discard payloads or rebuild an empty queue over unreadable data. V1 files migrate explicitly and save as v2.

ESubstrateTooOld.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ESubstrateTooOld.description: FR8: running kernel older than Spirit's declared min_substrate_version
ESubstrateTooOld.cause: The spirit manifest declares a `min_substrate_version` (per FR8) that is higher than the running kernel's version. The spirit requires a newer kernel than what is currently deployed.
ESubstrateTooOld.remediation: Upgrade the MAOS kernel to at least the version specified in the spirit's `min_substrate_version` field. Run `maos version` to check the current kernel version. Alternatively, if the spirit's requirement is overly strict, lower the `min_substrate_version` in the manifest.

ETeamIdInvalid.version_stability: stable within LTS cycle — no breaking error-code changes
ETeamIdInvalid.description: Operator-supplied team id failed the frozen lowercase ASCII tenant-identity grammar (ADR-055)
ETeamIdInvalid.cause: A team identifier is not already canonical lowercase ASCII [a-z0-9-] with a length of 2..=32 bytes. TeamId rejects uppercase letters, whitespace, Unicode, and other characters without normalizing signed identity material.
ETeamIdInvalid.remediation: Correct the team identifier at its authoritative configuration or manifest source to 2..=32 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or hyphens, and regenerate any signatures over changed material. Do not silently trim or lowercase an existing signed team identifier.
